message.content: {"name":"mortgage_property","arguments":{"space_key":"ATLANTIC_AVENUE","public_message":"Raising cash. The strip stays mine.","private_thought":"Follow the plan: mortgage Atlantic ($130), Marvin ($140), Pacific ($150), then even-build dark blues to 2/2 ($400). Cash now $221; after three mortgages ~$641, then ~$241 left. 2-house rents ($500/$600) threaten p4 ($61) and p2 ($174); 1-house rents do not. Keep ownership of yellows and Pacific so p4 cannot complete green or yellow. Do not trade cash or monopoly pieces. Roll from Ventnor is relatively safe (luxury tax $75, NC $16, GO TO JAIL). Emergency later: sell houses then mortgage dark blues if I hit oranges/pinks."}}
message.reasoning:
I need to make a Monopoly decision.

I have $221 and am on Ventnor Avenue. I recently paid $22 rent to p4 and mortgaged Electric Company for $75. My other properties are Atlantic, Marvin, and Pacific avenues plus Park Place and Boardwalk with one house each. p1 is in jail with $520 and owns the orange monopoly with two houses on St. James and Tennessee and three on New York. Kentucky and Indiana are mortgaged.

p2 has $174 and owns the pink monopoly with three houses each, though Illinois is mortgaged. p4 has $61 and owns hotels on Mediterranean and Baltic, plus railroads and a light blue monopoly with one house each. p4 also broke my yellow monopoly by landing on Ventnor.

I will mortgage Atlantic, Marvin, and Pacific avenues for $420. That brings my cash to $641. I can then build one more house on each dark blue property for $400. This leaves me with about $241.

I cannot afford three houses on each dark blue property. That would cost $800, but I only have $641. Even distribution is likely required by the game rules, so I will build one more house on each property to reach two houses each.

Uneven building is too risky. Two houses on Park Place and one on Boardwalk would cost $600 and leave only $41. Two houses each on both properties yield $500 and $600 in rent, which is significant against p2's $174 and p4's $61.

I will build the houses now before rolling. From Ventnor, rolling a 5 lands on Mediterranean with a hotel and costs $250. Rolling a 7 lands on Baltic with a hotel and costs $450. Rolling an 8 pays $200 in income tax. Rolling a 9 lands on Reading Railroad owned by p4 for $100.

Rolling a 10 lands on Oriental Avenue, which is part of p4's light blue monopoly. That property has zero houses, so the rent would be $12. Rolling an 11 lands on Chance. Rolling a 12 lands on Vermont Avenue.

The most dangerous spaces from Ventnor are Mediterranean with a hotel at $250, Baltic with a hotel at $450, Income Tax at $200, and Reading Railroad at $100.

I will not hit p1's orange properties or p2's pink properties this turn.

I mapped the exact board positions. From Ventnor, rolling a 1 lands on Water Works, which is mortgaged and costs nothing. Rolling a 2 lands on Marvin Gardens, which I own. Rolling a 3 sends me to Jail. Rolling a 4 lands on Pacific Avenue, also mine. Rolling a 5 lands on North Carolina, owned by p4 with no active monopoly. Rolling a 6 brings me to Community Chest. Rolling a 7 lands on Pennsylvania Avenue, which is mortgaged and costs nothing. Rolling an 8 lands on Short Line, which is unowned. Rolling a 9 brings me to Chance.

Rolling a 10 lands on Park Place, which I own but do not pay myself. Rolling an 11 lands on Luxury Tax for $75. Rolling a 12 lands on Boardwalk, also mine.

The only real danger from Ventnor is going to jail on roll 3. North Carolina costs only $16, and Chance or Community Chest are usually manageable.

This is relatively safe. I have already rolled and landed on Ventnor, so I am now in the post-turn action phase.

p4 is on Chance and will roll next. A two-house rent on Park Place or Boardwalk would cost p4 $500 or $600, far exceeding their $61 cash. They would have to liquidate hotels and railroads to pay. This immediate threat makes building now the right move.

p4 cannot land on Park Place from Chance. A roll of 1 is impossible with two dice. Boardwalk is reachable on a roll of 3, which would cost p4 $600. Selling hotels to pay that rent would force massive liquidation.

p1 is in jail with one turn already served, so they still have chances to roll doubles and escape. They are also already rich at $520.

p2 is on GO and cannot reach my dark blue properties this turn; landing on Park Place would require rolling 37.

I will not trade away the yellow properties. I cannot complete that monopoly without a trade anyway, and p4 is broke and unlikely to want them. Pacific Avenue should also stay mortgaged; it blocks p4's green monopoly.

I am verifying standard Monopoly rent tables to confirm the exact payouts for each house level on every property.

I have verified the standard rent tables for every property. The pink, orange, red, and yellow monopolies are now fully mapped with exact house-level payouts.

Two houses on Park Place and Boardwalk yield $500 and $600 in rent. Three houses raise those payouts to $1100 and $1400. p2's pink properties at three houses pay $450, $450, and $500. I will not land on them from Ventnor until I complete a full circuit. The only immediate danger is rolling a 3 to go to jail, which would place me near the pinks.

p1's orange properties at two and three houses pay $200, $200, and $600. I will have roughly $241 left after mortgaging and building. The immediate roll from Ventnor is low-risk. If I land on GO TO JAIL, I will be safe but start near the pinks when I leave.

I will not build three houses on one property and two on the other. That would leave only $41, which is too risky against luxury tax and rent. Even distribution is safer.

I considered trading for Ventnor Avenue to complete the yellow monopoly, but p4 is broke and hostile. They previously rejected an Electric-for-Ventnor offer, and giving them cash would help them survive my Boardwalk threat. I will not trade cash to p4.

I am now evaluating whether a trade with p1 is worthwhile.

No useful trades exist with p1 or p2. I will mortgage Atlantic, Marvin, and Pacific avenues now. Then I will build the houses and end my turn.

function.arguments: {"to_player_id":"p4","offer":{"cash":150,"properties":["ELECTRIC_COMPANY"],"get_out_of_jail_cards":0},"request":{"cash":0,"properties":["VENTNOR_AVENUE"],"get_out_of_jail_cards":0},"public_message":"p4, you are one bad roll from selling those hotels. Electric plus $150 for Ventnor — you get cash to survive Boardwalk and a utility you can unmortgage. I get a color I cannot build yet. Take it before the houses go up.","private_thought":"Cash is $221 after mortgaging Electric. A yellow monopoly is worth more than 2/2 dark blues if I can fund it, but $150 plus a mortgaged utility may not be enough for broke p4, and paying them cash funds survival on my own Boardwalk. Still worth one shot before I commit the mortgage-and-build plan: if they refuse, mortgage Atlantic/Marvin/Pacific and build 2/2 immediately. Do not sweeten further. Never give Pacific or the dark blues."}
